one_liner: Qt 6 web framework with its own epoll HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and FastCGI server; edges Drogon on HttpArena, trails nginx and actix-web.
what_it_does: A full-stack web framework modelled on Perl's Catalyst: controllers are QObject classes whose methods are tagged with C_ATTR attributes (:Local, :Path, :Chained, :AutoArgs), and Qt's meta-object system turns them into dispatchable actions at startup. It ships its own server engine (Cutelyst::Server) speaking HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive and pipelining, HTTP/2 (h2c, upgrade, ALPN), FastCGI and WebSockets, plus plugins for sessions, authentication, CSRF, validation, static files and Cutelee (Django-style) templates. It is a framework with its own API, not a drop-in for another server or framework.
how_it_is_fast: On Linux it replaces Qt's default event dispatcher with its own epoll-based one (EventLoopEPoll, using eventfd and timerfd) and runs one event loop per core, each with its own Application instance and, with reuse_port, its own SO_REUSEPORT listener so the kernel spreads connections without a shared accept lock. The HTTP/1.1 parser works in a fixed per-connection buffer, finds line ends with memchr and compacts pipelined requests with memmove, so the hot path avoids per-request allocations for the request head. Async handlers (ASync, QTimer, coroutines) hand responses back on the worker's own loop, which is why its 32,000-connection delay test scales across all cores.
when_to_use: You already build on Qt 6 (QString, QJsonDocument, Qt SQL or ASql) and want a web backend in the same stack with throughput in the same class as Drogon (2.15M vs 2.02M req/s on HttpArena baseline-4096).
Many idle or slow keep-alive connections served by async handlers on Linux: per-worker timers held 761,563 req/s over 32,000 connections with a 10 ms delay.
Pipelined HTTP/1.1 clients: 10.17M req/s on HttpArena's 16-deep pipelined profile, above Drogon (7.80M) and nginx (4.04M).
Apps that want Catalyst-style chained dispatch, sessions, auth and templates in one BSD-3-Clause package, deployed directly or behind a front proxy via FastCGI.
when_not_to_use: Maximum raw throughput: on the same HttpArena board nginx (3.28M) and actix-web (2.78M req/s) beat Cutelyst's 2.15M on baseline-4096, and on json-tls-4096 nginx, h2o and actix serve 3.5-4x more (1.31M, 1.23M, 1.16M vs 326,846); even Express is ahead there (394,866).
TLS JSON APIs that care about tail latency: Cutelyst's json-tls-4096 p99 was 478 ms against Drogon's 117 ms, despite higher mean throughput.

Fixed-rate, latency-sensitive serving at moderate load: Drogon had lower mean latency and CPU at 1M req/s (108.1 us, 3551.7% vs 137.6 us, 3825.6%) and served more on latency-500k-8cpu (374,962 vs 329,347 req/s).
Projects that cannot take a Qt 6 runtime dependency or a C++23 compiler (README asks for g++-14 or newer; Clang builds are forced onto libc++).

Database-backed pages if you rely on HttpArena for evidence: its async-db and fortunes rows (384 req/s) measure a misconfigured entry, so Cutelyst's DB performance is unmeasured rather than shown to be good or bad.

integration.dependencies: Qt 6.5+ (Core, Network; Sql and LinguistTools at build time), CMake 3.28+; optional Cutelee (templates), ASql (async PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite), libmemcached, libpwquality
integration.min_toolchain: C++23 (README: g++-14 or newer); CMake 3.28; Clang builds add -stdlib=libc++ for coroutines
integration.platforms: Linux (custom epoll event loop, SO_REUSEPORT, process forking), plus other Qt platforms including Windows (recent Windows server fixes); 'cross-platform' per README
integration.thread_safety: Server creates one Application (and controller set) per worker thread when the app constructor is Q_INVOKABLE and threads > 1; each thread runs its own event loop, so state shared across threads is the user's responsibility. README warns that local QEventLoops in async code will eventually crash.

gotchas: Harness flaw behind HttpArena's database rows: the entry (frameworks/cutelyst/app.cpp) gives each worker thread an ASql pool of min(240, DATABASE_MAX_CONN)/idealThreadCount connections (3 per thread with 64 threads) and calls enterPipelineMode(500 ms), which in ASql's Postgres driver arms a single-shot timer that sends PQpipelineSync only every 500 ms. Each pooled connection therefore completes one query per sync tick: 64 x 3 x 2/s = 384 req/s, exactly the async-db-1024 and fortunes-1024 results (fortunes: 1,920 responses in 5 s = 192 connections x 10 ticks), with 2.0-2.3 s mean latency from 1,024 clients queueing for 192 connections (derived from page data and source). Those rows measure the entry's sync timer, not Cutelyst or ASql.

The benchmarked server is not a release: HttpArena builds upstream commit 5ec5ce9 (2026-09-11, 'Add http chunked for HttpArena benchmarks', +171 lines in protocolhttp.cpp), which added Transfer-Encoding: chunked request-body parsing for the first time. The latest tag v5.1.0 and its Ubuntu .deb (the entry's runtime base before the overlay) cannot parse chunked request bodies.

The whole request head must fit in buffer_size (default 4096 bytes). When the buffer fills, protocolhttp.cpp reaches an empty block commented '414 Request-URI Too Long' and sends nothing, so requests with large cookies or bearer tokens appear to hang (read from source, not tested); raise buffer_size (the HttpArena entry uses 128 KiB).

Robustness history: issue #379 (closed December 2022) reported a malformed HTTP/1.0 POST whose body was longer than its Content-Length making the whole server unresponsive until kill -9; issue #146 (Ctrl+C abort crash) and #214 (SIGTERM handling) are still open.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against Drogon, its closest C++ sibling, throughput is within 2-6% on HttpArena's scored HTTP/1.1 profiles, so pick Cutelyst when your code is already Qt and you want Catalyst-style dispatch, HTTP/2 and FastCGI in one engine, and Drogon when you want no Qt dependency. For maximum req/s look at h2o, Sogou Workflow or Lithium instead, and for a small embeddable server Crow or cpp-httplib.
verified_claims_summary: On HttpArena (AMD Threadripper PRO 3995WX, server container pinned to 32 cores plus SMT siblings, gcannon load generator on the remaining CPUs, best of three 5 s runs), Cutelyst built from upstream commit 5ec5ce9 with Ubuntu 26.04's g++ in Release mode served 2,153,860 req/s on baseline-4096 vs Drogon's 2,022,710 (1.06x), 1.02x on limited-conn, 1.29x on json-tls and 1.30x on the reference-only pipelined profile; Drogon's rows are a month older and built with g++-11 on an unpinned image, and the 5.3x async row reflects the Drogon entry running all timers on one loop. nginx and actix-web on the same board are faster on the main profiles.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-11, latest tag v5.1.0) and BSD-3-Clause, so copyable, but the HttpArena numbers come from an unreleased master commit written for the benchmark by Cutelyst's own author, and its database rows are invalid because the entry's 500 ms pipeline auto-sync caps them at 384 req/s.
